sourceDate.text: 歲餘 after 元朔五年

label.en: Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince

units.zh: 萬石君名奮，其父趙人也，姓石氏。
units.en: The Marquis of Wanshi was named Fen. His father was a man of Zhao, surnamed Shi.
units.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi was named Fen, his father was from Zhao, surname Shi.

units.zh: 趙亡，徙居溫。
units.en: When Zhao fell, he moved to Wen.
units.literal: After Zhao perished, he moved to reside in Wen.

units.zh: 高祖東擊項籍，過河內，時奮年十五，為小吏，侍高祖。
units.en: When Gaozu marched east to attack Xiang Ji and passed through Henei, Fen was fifteen years old, serving as a minor functionary in attendance on Gaozu.
units.literal: When Gaozu struck east against Xiang Ji, passing through Henei, at that time Fen was fifteen years old, serving as a minor official attending Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖與語，愛其恭敬，問曰：「若何有？」
units.en: Gaozu spoke with him and was pleased by his respectful bearing. He asked, "What do you have?"
units.literal: Gaozu spoke with him and was pleased by his respectful bearing, and asked, "What do you have?"

units.zh: 對曰：「奮獨有母，不幸失明。
units.en: He replied, "I have only my mother, who has unfortunately gone blind.
units.literal: He replied, "Fen has only a mother, who has unfortunately gone blind.

units.zh: 家貧。
units.en: His family was poor.
units.literal: The family is poor.

units.zh: 有姊，能鼓琴。」
units.en: I also have an elder sister who can play the zither."
units.literal: I have an elder sister who can play the zither."

units.zh: 高祖曰：「若能從我乎？」
units.en: Gaozu said, "Can you follow me?"
units.literal: Gaozu said, "Can you follow me?"

units.zh: 曰：「願盡力。」
units.en: He said, "I will do my utmost."
units.literal: He said, "I wish to serve with all my strength."

units.zh: 於是高祖召其姊為美人，以奮為中涓，受書謁，徙其家長安中戚裏，以姊為美人故也。
units.en: Thereupon Gaozu summoned his elder sister to serve as a court beauty, appointed Fen as a palace attendant in charge of receiving documents and audiences, and relocated his family to the Zhongqi quarter in Chang'an—all on account of his sister becoming a court beauty.
units.literal: Then Gaozu summoned his elder sister to become a beauty, made Fen a palace attendant receiving documents and audiences, moved his family to the Zhongqi quarter in Chang'an, because his elder sister became a beauty.

units.zh: 其官至孝文時，積功勞至大中大夫。
units.en: By the time of Emperor Wen, he had accumulated enough merit to rise to the rank of Grand Palace Counselor.
units.literal: His official position reached during Emperor Wen's time, accumulating merit he reached Grand Palace Counselor.

units.zh: 無文學，恭謹無與比。
units.en: He had no literary learning, but in respectful caution he was without equal.
units.literal: Without literary learning, his respectful caution had no equal.

units.zh: 文帝時，東陽侯張相如為太子太傅，免。
units.en: During Emperor Wen's reign, the Marquis of Dongyang, Zhang Xiangru, served as Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince but was dismissed.
units.literal: During Emperor Wen's time, the Marquis of Dongyang Zhang Xiangru served as crown prince's Grand Tutor, was dismissed.

units.zh: 選可為傅者，皆推奮，奮為太子太傅。
units.en: When a suitable replacement was being selected, all recommended Fen, and so Fen became Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: When selecting someone suitable as tutor, all recommended Fen, so Fen became crown prince's Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 及孝景即位，以為九卿；
units.en: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, he was appointed one of the Nine Ministers;
units.literal: When Emperor Jing ascended the throne, [Fen] was appointed one of the Nine Ministers;

units.zh: 迫近，憚之，徙奮為諸侯相。
units.en: Being too close to the throne, others feared him, and so Fen was transferred to serve as chancellor of a feudal kingdom.
units.literal: Pressing close, they feared him, transferred Fen to become chancellor of feudal lords.

units.zh: 奮長子建，次子甲，次子乙，次子慶，皆以馴行孝謹，官皆至二千石。
units.en: Fen's eldest son Jian, second son Jia, third son Yi, and fourth son Qing all attained the rank of two-thousand-bushel official through their disciplined conduct, filial piety, and caution.
units.literal: Fen's eldest son Jian, second son Jia, third son Yi, fourth son Qing, all through their tame conduct filial piety and caution, their official positions all reached two thousand dan.

units.zh: 於是景帝曰：「石君及四子皆二千石，人臣尊寵乃集其門。」
units.en: Emperor Jing therefore said, "Lord Shi and his four sons all hold offices of two thousand bushels. The honor and favor due to ministers are gathered at his gate."
units.literal: Thereupon Emperor Jing said, "Lord Shi and his four sons are all two-thousand-bushel officials—ministerial honor and favor all gather at his gate."

units.zh: 號奮為萬石君。
units.en: He bestowed upon Fen the title Marquis of Wanshi.
units.literal: He titled Fen the Marquis of Wan Shi.

units.zh: 孝景帝季年，萬石君以上大夫祿歸老于家，以歲時為朝臣。
units.en: In the later years of Emperor Jing's reign, the Marquis of Wanshi retired to his home on the salary of a Senior Grand Counselor, attending court only at seasonal assemblies.
units.literal: In the later years of Emperor Jing, the Marquis of Wan Shi returned home to retire on the salary of Grand Palace Counselor, serving as court minister by season.

units.zh: 過宮門闕，萬石君必下車趨，見路馬必式焉。
units.en: Whenever he passed the gate-towers of the palace, the Marquis of Wanshi would invariably step down from his carriage and walk briskly past. Whenever he saw the imperial carriage horses on the road, he would bow in salute.
units.literal: Passing the palace gate towers, the Marquis of Wan Shi would certainly descend his chariot and hasten, seeing road horses he would certainly salute.

units.zh: 子孫為小吏，來歸謁，萬石君必朝服見之，不名。
units.en: When his sons and grandsons who served as minor officials came home to pay their respects, the Marquis of Wanshi would invariably receive them in full court dress, never addressing them by name.
units.literal: When sons and grandsons serving as minor officials came home to visit, the Marquis of Wan Shi would certainly wear court robes to see them, not using names.

units.zh: 子孫有過失，不譙讓，為便坐，對案不食。
units.en: When his sons and grandsons committed errors, he would not scold or reproach them but would take his seat, face the table, and refuse to eat.
units.literal: When sons and grandsons had faults, he would not scold or reproach them but would take his seat, face the table, and not eat.

units.zh: 然後諸子相責，因長老肉袒固謝罪，改之，乃許。
units.en: Then the sons would reproach one another, and the elders would bare their shoulders and earnestly beg forgiveness. Only when the offender had reformed would he relent.
units.literal: Then the various sons would mutually reproach each other, because of the elders stripping to the waist and firmly apologizing for the offense, changing it, then he would allow it.

units.zh: 子孫勝冠者在側，雖燕居必冠，申申如也。
units.en: When sons and grandsons who had undergone the capping ceremony were at his side, he would always wear his cap even in private, bearing himself with grave composure.
units.literal: When sons and grandsons who had undergone the capping ceremony were at his side, even in private he would always wear his cap, grave and composed.

units.zh: 僮仆訢訢如也，唯謹。
units.en: His servants and attendants went about cheerfully, all with the utmost caution.
units.literal: The servants and attendants were cheerful and only cautious.

units.zh: 上時賜食於家，必稽首俯伏而食之，如在上前。
units.en: Whenever the emperor bestowed food upon his household, he would invariably bow his head to the ground and prostrate himself before eating it, as though he were in the emperor's presence.
units.literal: When the emperor occasionally granted food at home, he would certainly bow his head and prostrate to eat it, as if before the emperor.

units.zh: 其執喪，哀戚甚悼。
units.en: When the family observed mourning, their grief was profound and deeply sorrowful.
units.literal: Their observance of mourning was sorrowfully sad and deeply mournful.

units.zh: 子孫遵教，亦如之。
units.en: His sons and grandsons followed his teachings and conducted themselves in the same manner.
units.literal: Sons and grandsons followed the teachings, also like this.

units.zh: 萬石君家以孝謹聞乎郡國，雖齊魯諸儒質行，皆自以為不及也。
units.en: The household of the Marquis of Wanshi was renowned for filial piety and caution throughout the commanderies and kingdoms. Even the Confucian scholars of Qi and Lu, known for their upright conduct, all considered themselves his inferiors.
units.literal: The Wan Shi Jun household was known for filial piety and caution throughout commanderies and kingdoms, though the various Confucian scholars of Qi and Lu in solid conduct, all considered themselves not equal.

units.zh: 建元二年，郎中令王臧以文學獲罪。
units.en: In the second year of the Jianyuan era, the Palace Steward Wang Zang was convicted on account of his literary activities.
units.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, the Palace Steward Wang Zang was convicted for literary matters.

units.zh: 皇太后以為儒者文多質少，今萬石君家不言而躬行，乃以長子建為郎中令，少子慶為內史。
units.en: The Empress Dowager considered that Confucian scholars were long on rhetoric but short on substance, whereas the household of the Marquis of Wanshi spoke little but practiced virtue in person. She therefore appointed the eldest son Jian as Palace Steward and the youngest son Qing as Interior Minister.
units.literal: The Empress Dowager considered scholars have much text but little substance, now the Wan Shi Jun household does not speak but practices with their bodies, so she made the eldest son Jian Palace Steward, the youngest son Qing Interior Minister.

units.zh: 建老白首，萬石君尚無恙。
units.en: By the time Jian had grown old and white-haired, the Marquis of Wanshi was still in good health.
units.literal: Jian grew old with white hair, the Marquis of Wan Shi was still without illness.

units.zh: 建為郎中令，每五日洗沐歸謁親，入子舍，竊問侍者，取親中帬廁牏，身自浣滌，復與侍者，不敢令萬石君知，以為常。
units.en: While serving as Palace Steward, Jian would return home every five days during his rest period to visit his parents. He would slip into the servants' quarters, secretly ask for his father's undergarments and chamber-pot linings, wash them himself, then return them to the servants—never daring to let the Marquis of Wanshi know. This became his constant practice.
units.literal: Jian served as Palace Steward, every five days he would wash and bathe then return home to visit his parents, entering the children's quarters, secretly asking the servants, taking the parents' jackets and toilet mats, personally washing and cleaning them, then returning them to the servants, not daring to let the Marquis of Wan Shi know, making it his constant practice.

units.zh: 建為郎中令，事有可言，屏人恣言，極切；
units.en: While serving as Palace Steward, when there was something worth saying on state affairs, he would dismiss attendants and speak with utmost frankness and force;
units.literal: As Palace Steward, when there was something worth saying on state affairs, he would dismiss attendants and speak with unrestrained frankness, extremely pointed;

units.zh: 至廷見，如不能言者。
units.en: Yet at court audiences, he appeared as though he could not speak a word.
units.literal: When reaching court audiences, he was like one unable to speak.

units.zh: 是以上乃親尊禮之。
units.en: For this reason, the emperor personally honored him and treated him with the highest respect.
units.literal: Therefore, the emperor personally honored and ritualized him.

units.zh: 萬石君徙居陵裏。
units.en: The Marquis of Wanshi moved his residence to the Ling quarter.
units.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi moved to reside in Ling quarter.

units.zh: 內史慶醉歸，入外門不下車。
units.en: The Interior Minister Qing returned home drunk and entered the outer gate without descending from his carriage.
units.literal: The Interior Minister Qing returned drunk, entering the outer gate without descending his chariot.

units.zh: 萬石君聞之，不食。
units.en: When the Marquis of Wanshi heard of this, he refused to eat.
units.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi heard of it and would not eat.

units.zh: 慶恐，肉袒請罪，不許。
units.en: Qing was frightened and bared his shoulders to beg forgiveness, but the Marquis would not accept.
units.literal: Qing feared, stripped to the waist and apologized for the offense, but was not allowed.

units.zh: 舉宗及兄建肉袒，萬石君讓曰：「內史貴人，入閭里，里中長老皆走匿，而內史坐車中自如，固當！」
units.en: The whole clan, together with his elder brother Jian, bared their shoulders. The Marquis of Wanshi rebuked him, saying, "The Interior Minister is an exalted man: when he enters the lane, the elders there all run and hide, while the Interior Minister sits calmly in his carriage. Quite proper!"
units.literal: The whole clan and his elder brother Jian bared their shoulders. The Marquis of Wanshi rebuked him, saying, "The Interior Minister is a man of rank. When he enters the lane, the elders of the lane all flee and hide, yet the Interior Minister sits at ease in his carriage—as he ought!"

units.zh: 乃謝罷慶。
units.en: Only then did he forgive and dismiss Qing.
units.literal: Then he thanked and dismissed Qing.

units.zh: 慶及諸子弟入里門，趨至家。
units.en: From then on, Qing and all the sons and younger brothers would enter the quarter gate and hasten home on foot.
units.literal: Qing and the various sons and younger brothers entered the quarter gate, hastening home.

units.zh: 萬石君以元朔五年中卒。
units.en: The Marquis of Wanshi died in the fifth year of the Yuanshuo era.
units.literal: The Marquis of Wan Shi died in the middle of the fifth year of Yuanshuo.

units.zh: 長子郎中令建哭泣哀思，扶杖乃能行。
units.en: His eldest son, the Palace Steward Jian, wept so piteously in his grief that he could walk only by leaning on a staff.
units.literal: The eldest son Palace Steward Jian wept and mourned sorrowfully, supporting a staff he could then walk.

units.zh: 歲餘，建亦死。
units.en: A little over a year later, Jian too died.
units.literal: Over a year later, Jian also died.

units.zh: 諸子孫咸孝，然建最甚，甚於萬石君。
units.en: All the sons and grandsons were filial, but Jian was the most extreme of all—surpassing even the Marquis of Wanshi himself.
units.literal: All the sons and grandsons were filial, but Jian was most extreme, even more than the Marquis of Wan Shi.

units.zh: 建為郎中令，書奏事，事下，建讀之，曰：「誤書！
units.en: While Jian was serving as Palace Steward, memorials on affairs came down to him. He read one and said, "There is an error in the writing!
units.literal: While serving as Palace Steward, when memorials on affairs came down, Jian read them and said, "An error in the document!

units.zh: 『馬』者與尾當五，今乃四，不足一。
units.en: The graph for 'horse' ought to have five strokes in the tail, but here there are only four; one is missing.
units.literal: The character for 'horse' should have five strokes in the tail; now there are only four—one stroke short.

units.zh: 上譴死矣！」
units.en: The emperor will blame me to death!"
units.literal: The emperor will blame me to death!"

units.zh: 甚惶恐。
units.en: He was greatly alarmed and fearful.
units.literal: He was greatly panicked and fearful.

units.zh: 其為謹慎，雖他皆如是。
units.en: Such was his caution—and in all other matters he was just the same.
units.literal: His being cautious and careful, though others were all like this.

units.zh: 萬石君少子慶為太仆，御出，上問車中幾馬，慶以策數馬畢，舉手曰：「六馬。」
units.en: The Marquis of Wanshi's youngest son Qing served as Grand Coachman. When he drove out with the emperor, the emperor asked how many horses were in the carriage. Qing counted the horses with his whip, then raised his hand and said, "Six horses."
units.literal: The Marquis of Wanshi's youngest son Qing served as Grand Coachman. When he drove out with the emperor, the emperor asked how many horses were in the carriage. Qing finished counting the horses with his whip, raised his hand, and said, "Six horses."

units.zh: 慶於諸子中最為簡易矣，然猶如此。
units.en: Qing was the most casual and easygoing among the sons, yet even he behaved this way.
units.literal: Qing among the various sons was the most simple and easy, yet still like this.

units.zh: 為齊相，舉齊國皆慕其家行，不言而齊國大治，為立石相祠。
units.en: When he served as Chancellor of Qi, the entire kingdom admired his family's conduct. Without a word of command, Qi was brought to excellent order, and the people erected a stone shrine to Chancellor Shi in his honor.
units.literal: Serving as Chancellor of Qi, he led the whole state to admire his family's conduct; without speaking [commands], Qi was brought to excellent order, and they erected a shrine to Chancellor Shi.

units.zh: 元狩元年，上立太子，選群臣可為傅者，慶自沛守為太子太傅，七歲遷為御史大夫。
units.en: In the first year of the Yuanshou era, the emperor established the Crown Prince and selected from among his ministers those fit to serve as tutor. Qing was transferred from his post as Governor of Pei to become Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, and after seven years was promoted to Imperial Secretary.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanshou, the emperor established the crown prince, selecting ministers suitable as tutors, Qing from Pei governor became crown prince's Grand Tutor, after seven years was promoted to Imperial Secretary.

units.zh: 元鼎五年秋，丞相有罪，罷。
units.en: In the autumn of the fifth year of the Yuanding era, the Chancellor was found guilty and dismissed.
units.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Yuanding, the Chancellor had crime, was dismissed.

units.zh: 制詔御史：「萬石君先帝尊之，子孫孝，其以御史大夫慶為丞相，封為牧丘侯。」
units.en: The emperor issued an edict to the Imperial Secretary: "The Marquis of Wanshi was honored by the former emperor, and his sons and grandsons are filial. Let the Imperial Secretary Qing become Chancellor, and let him be enfeoffed as Marquis of Muqiu."
units.literal: An imperial edict to the Imperial Secretary: "The Marquis of Wanshi was honored by the former emperor, and his sons and grandsons are filial. Let the Imperial Secretary Qing be made Chancellor and enfeoffed as Marquis of Muqiu."

units.zh: 是時漢方南誅兩越，東擊朝鮮，北逐匈奴，西伐大宛，中國多事。
units.en: At this time, the Han was campaigning against the two Yue kingdoms in the south, striking Chaoxian in the east, pursuing the Xiongnu in the north, and attacking Dayuan in the west. The empire was beset with affairs.
units.literal: At this time Han was just punishing the two Yue in the south, striking Chaoxian in the east, pursuing the Xiongnu in the north, attacking Dayuan in the west, China had many affairs.

units.zh: 天子巡狩海內，修上古神祠，封禪，興禮樂。
units.en: The emperor toured and hunted throughout the realm, restored the ancient divine shrines, performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices, and revived the rites and music.
units.literal: The emperor toured and hunted within the seas, repaired the ancient god temples, performed the Feng and Shan sacrifices, raised rites and music.

units.zh: 公家用少，桑弘羊等致利，王溫舒之屬峻法，兒寬等推文學至九卿，更進用事，事不關決於丞相，丞相醇謹而已。
units.en: The state coffers were running low. Sang Hongyang and his like raised revenue, Wang Wenshu and his sort enforced harsh laws, and Er Kuan and others advanced through scholarship to the rank of the Nine Ministers. Those who handled affairs were the ones promoted, and decisions were no longer referred to the Chancellor. The Chancellor was simply upright and cautious, nothing more.
units.literal: Public family expenditures were few, Sang Hongyang and others achieved profits, Wang Wenshu and others enforced severe laws, Er Kuan and others promoted literature to reach the Nine Ministers, changing to advance those who handled affairs, affairs not closely decided by the Chancellor, the Chancellor was pure and cautious only.

units.zh: 在位九歲，無能有所匡言。
units.en: In nine years in office, he was never able to offer a single word of correction.
units.literal: In position nine years, unable to have any rectifying words.

units.zh: 嘗欲請治上近臣所忠、九卿咸宣罪，不能服，反受其過，贖罪。
units.en: He once sought to have the emperor's close minister Suo Zhong prosecuted and the crimes of the Nine Ministers publicly declared, but could not prevail; instead he himself bore the blame and had to ransom his offense.
units.literal: He once wished to request prosecution of the emperor's close minister Suo Zhong and public announcement of the crimes of the Nine Ministers, but could not prevail; instead he himself bore the blame and had to ransom his offense.

units.zh: 元封四年中，關東流民二百萬口，無名數者四十萬，公卿議欲請徙流民於邊以適之。
units.en: In the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, there were two million displaced refugees east of the passes, with another four hundred thousand unregistered. The ministers debated whether to petition for the refugees to be relocated to the frontier.
units.literal: In the fourth year of the Yuanfeng era, there were two million displaced people east of the passes, with another four hundred thousand unregistered; the ministers debated petitioning to relocate the refugees to the frontier.

units.zh: 上以為丞相老謹，不能與其議，乃賜丞相告歸，而案御史大夫以下議為請者。
units.en: The emperor considered the Chancellor old and overly cautious, unable to take part in such deliberations, and so granted the Chancellor leave to retire. He then investigated the Imperial Secretary and those below who had proposed the petition.
units.literal: The emperor considered the Chancellor old and cautious, could not discuss with him, so granted the Chancellor to announce his retirement, and investigated the Imperial Secretary and below who had discussed and requested this.

units.zh: 丞相慚不任職，乃上書曰：「慶幸得待罪丞相，罷駑無以輔治，城郭倉庫空虛，民多流亡，罪當伏斧質，上不忍致法。
units.en: The Chancellor, ashamed that he could not fulfill his duties, submitted a memorial saying, "Qing has had the good fortune to serve as Chancellor while awaiting punishment; I am worn out and incapable of assisting in governance. The walled cities and storehouses are empty, and the people are fleeing in great numbers. My crime deserves execution by axe, yet Your Majesty has been unwilling to apply the law.
units.literal: The Chancellor, ashamed that he could not bear his duties, submitted a memorial saying, "Qing has had the good fortune to serve as Chancellor while awaiting punishment; I am worn out and incapable of assisting in governance. The walled cities and storehouses are empty, and the people are fleeing in great numbers. My crime deserves execution by axe, yet Your Majesty has been unwilling to apply the law.

units.zh: 願歸丞相侯印，乞骸骨歸，避賢者路。」
units.en: I wish to return the Chancellor's seal and my marquisate, beg leave to retire, and make way for worthier men."
units.literal: I wish to return the Chancellor's seal and the marquisate, beg to retire with my bones, and yield the road to the worthy."

units.zh: 天子曰：「倉廩既空，民貧流亡，而君欲請徙之，搖蕩不安，動危之，而辭位，君欲安歸難乎？」
units.en: The emperor said, "The granaries are already empty and the people poor and displaced—yet you wished to petition to relocate them, which would shake and unsettle them and expose them to danger; yet you resign your post—where do you intend to go to escape difficulty?"
units.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "The granaries are already empty and the people poor and displaced—yet you wished to petition to relocate them, which would shake and unsettle them and expose them to danger; yet you resign your post—where do you intend to go to escape difficulty?"

units.zh: 以書讓慶，慶甚慚，遂復視事。
units.en: He rebuked Qing by letter. Qing was deeply ashamed and thereupon resumed his duties.
units.literal: He rebuked Qing by letter; Qing was very ashamed, then again oversaw affairs.

units.zh: 慶文深審謹，然無他大略，為百姓言。
units.en: Qing was learned, thorough, and cautious, yet he had no grand strategies to offer and spoke only on behalf of the common people.
units.literal: Qing was cultured deeply examining and cautious, yet had no other great strategies, spoke for the people.

units.zh: 後三歲餘，太初二年中，丞相慶卒，謚為恬侯。
units.en: A little over three years later, in the second year of the Taichu era, Chancellor Qing died and was posthumously titled Marquis Tian.
units.literal: After three years remaining, in the middle of the second year of Taichu, Chancellor Qing died, posthumous title Marquis Tian.

units.zh: 慶中子德，慶愛用之，上以德為嗣，代侯。
units.en: Qing's second son De was beloved and favored by Qing. The emperor appointed De as his heir to succeed as marquis.
units.literal: Qing's middle son De, Qing loved and used him, the emperor made De his successor, replacing as Marquis.

units.zh: 後為太常，坐法當死，贖免為庶人。
units.en: He later served as Grand Master of Ceremonies but was convicted of a capital offense. He ransomed himself and was reduced to a commoner.
units.literal: Afterward became Grand Master of Ceremonies, convicted by law should die, redeemed and freed to become commoner.

units.zh: 慶方為丞相，諸子孫為吏更至二千石者十三人。
units.en: When Qing first became Chancellor, thirteen of his sons and grandsons had attained the rank of two-thousand-bushel officials.
units.literal: When Qing just became Chancellor, his various sons and grandsons who became officials reaching two thousand dan were thirteen people.

units.zh: 及慶死後，稍以罪去，孝謹益衰矣。
units.en: After Qing's death, they gradually fell from office due to offenses, and the family's tradition of filial caution steadily declined.
units.literal: When Qing died, gradually they left due to crimes, filial caution increasingly declined.

units.zh: 建陵侯衛綰者，代大陵人也。
units.en: The Marquis of Jianling, Wei Wan, was a man of Daling in Dai.
units.literal: The Marquis of Jianling Wei Wan was a person from Daling in Dai.

units.zh: 綰以戲車為郎，事文帝，功次遷為中郎將，醇謹無他。
units.en: Wan entered service as a mounted attendant through his skill in chariot games, serving Emperor Wen. Through accumulated merit he was successively promoted to Colonel of the Palace Guard—upright and cautious, with no other notable qualities.
units.literal: Wan became a mounted attendant through chariot games, served Emperor Wen, merit successively promoted to Colonel, pure and cautious without other qualities.

units.zh: 孝景為太子時，召上左右飲，而綰稱病不行。
units.en: When Emperor Jing was still Crown Prince, he summoned Emperor Wen's attendants to drink with him, but Wan pleaded illness and did not go.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing was Crown Prince, he summoned the attendants of the emperor [Wen] to drink, but Wan pleaded illness and did not go.

units.zh: 文帝且崩時，屬孝景曰：「綰長者，善遇之。」
units.en: When Emperor Wen was near death, he charged Emperor Jing, saying, "Wan is a man of mature character. Treat him well."
units.literal: When Emperor Wen was about to die, he entrusted Emperor Jing, saying, "Wan is a man of mature character—treat him well."

units.zh: 及文帝崩，景帝立，歲餘不噍呵綰，綰日以謹力。
units.en: After Emperor Wen died and Emperor Jing ascended the throne, more than a year passed without his ever scolding or rebuking Wan. Wan redoubled his cautious diligence each day.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen passed away and Emperor Jing ascended, over a year did not scold or berate Wan, Wan daily exerted himself cautiously.

units.zh: 景帝幸上林，詔中郎將參乘，還而問曰：「君知所以得參乘乎？」
units.en: Emperor Jing visited Shanglin Park and ordered the Colonel of the Palace Guard to ride beside him in the imperial carriage. On the return, he asked, "Do you know why you were given this place beside me?"
units.literal: Emperor Jing visited Shanglin Park and ordered the Colonel of the Palace Guard to ride beside him as attendant. On the return he asked, "Do you know why you were granted the place of attendant in the carriage?"

units.zh: 綰曰：「臣從車士幸得以功次遷為中郎將，不自知也。」
units.en: Wan said, "Your servant began as a chariot soldier and was fortunate enough to be promoted by degrees to Colonel of the Palace Guard. I do not know the reason."
units.literal: Wan said, "Your servant followed as a chariot warrior and was fortunate to be promoted step by step to Colonel of the Palace Guard—I do not know [why]."

units.zh: 上問曰：「吾為太子時召君，君不肯來，何也？」
units.en: The emperor asked, "When I was Crown Prince, I summoned you, but you refused to come. Why?"
units.literal: The emperor asked, "When I was Crown Prince I summoned you, but you were unwilling to come—why?"

units.zh: 對曰：「死罪，實病！」
units.en: He replied, "I deserve death, but I truly was ill!"
units.literal: He replied, "A capital offense—I was truly ill!"

units.zh: 上賜之劍。
units.en: The emperor bestowed a sword upon him.
units.literal: The emperor granted him a sword.

units.zh: 綰曰：「先帝賜臣劍凡六，劍不敢奉詔。」
units.en: Wan said, "The former emperor granted me six swords in all; I dare not comply with the edict [to wear this one]."
units.literal: Wan said, "The former emperor granted your servant six swords in all; your servant dares not comply with the edict [to wear this one]."

units.zh: 上曰：「劍，人之所施易，獨至今乎？」
units.en: The emperor said, "Swords are things people readily give away. Can it be that you alone have kept yours down to the present?"
units.literal: The emperor said, "Swords are what men part with readily—have you alone kept yours until now?"

units.zh: 綰曰：「具在。」
units.en: Wan said, "They are all here."
units.literal: Wan said, "They are all here."

units.zh: 上使取六劍，劍尚盛，未嘗服也。
units.en: The emperor had the six swords brought out. They were still in pristine condition—he had never once worn them.
units.literal: The emperor had the six swords taken, the swords were still abundant, he had never used them.

units.zh: 郎官有譴，常蒙其罪，不與他將爭；
units.en: When palace attendants were reprimanded, he often shielded them by taking the blame himself, and he did not quarrel with other commanders;
units.literal: When palace attendants were blamed, he would regularly shield them and bear their guilt, and would not dispute with other commanders;

units.zh: 有功，常讓他將。
units.en: When there was merit to be claimed, he always deferred to the other generals.
units.literal: When there was merit, he constantly yielded to other generals.

units.zh: 上以為廉，忠實無他腸，乃拜綰為河閒王太傅。
units.en: The emperor considered him incorruptible, loyal, and sincere, without any ulterior motives, and so appointed Wan as Grand Tutor to the King of Hejian.
units.literal: The emperor considered him clean, loyal and real without other intentions, then appointed Wan as Hejian King's Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 吳楚反，詔綰為將，將河閒兵擊吳楚有功，拜為中尉。
units.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, an edict appointed Wan as general. He led the troops of Hejian against Wu and Chu with distinction, and was appointed Commandant.
units.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, an edict appointed Wan as general; he led the troops of Hejian against Wu and Chu with merit and was appointed Commandant of the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 三歲，以軍功，孝景前六年中封綰為建陵侯。
units.en: Three years later, on account of his military merit, in the sixth year of Emperor Jing's first reign period, Wan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianling.
units.literal: Three years, through army merit, in the middle of the sixth year of Emperor Jing's reign before his death, sealed Wan as Marquis of Jianling.

units.zh: 其明年，上廢太子，誅栗卿之屬。
units.en: The following year, the emperor deposed the Crown Prince and executed Li Qing and his associates.
units.literal: The next year, the emperor deposed the crown prince, executed Li Qing and his group.

units.zh: 上以為綰長者，不忍，乃賜綰告歸，而使郅都治捕栗氏。
units.en: The emperor regarded Wan as a venerable elder who could not bear such matters, and so granted Wan leave to retire. He then dispatched Zhi Du to arrest the Li clan.
units.literal: The emperor considered Wan a venerable elder, could not bear it, so granted Wan to announce retirement, and had Zhi Du govern and catch the Li clan.

units.zh: 既已，上立膠東王為太子，召綰，拜為太子太傅。
units.en: When this was done, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as Crown Prince, summoned Wan, and appointed him Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: Afterward, the emperor established the King of Jiaodong as crown prince, summoned Wan, appointed him crown prince's Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 久之，遷為御史大夫。
units.en: After a long while, he was promoted to Imperial Secretary.
units.literal: After a long time, promoted to Imperial Secretary.

units.zh: 五歲，代桃侯舍為丞相，朝奏事如職所奏。
units.en: Five years later, he succeeded She, Marquis of Tao, as Chancellor, and presented memorials at court according to the duties of his office.
units.literal: After five years, he replaced the Marquis of Tao, She, as Chancellor, presenting memorials at court as the duties of his office required.

units.zh: 然自初官以至丞相，終無可言。
units.en: Yet from his first appointment as an official all the way to the chancellorship, he ultimately had nothing worth saying.
units.literal: Yet from beginning as official until Chancellor, ultimately had nothing to say.

units.zh: 天子以為敦厚，可相少主，尊寵之，賞賜甚多。
units.en: The emperor considered him sincere and steadfast, fit to serve as Chancellor for a young ruler, and honored and favored him greatly, bestowing many rewards and gifts.
units.literal: The emperor considered him sincere and substantial, able to be Chancellor for the young ruler, honored and favored him, rewards and grants very many.

units.zh: 為丞相三歲，景帝崩，武帝立。
units.en: After three years as Chancellor, Emperor Jing died and Emperor Wu ascended the throne.
units.literal: Served as Chancellor three years, Emperor Jing passed away, Emperor Wu ascended.

units.zh: 建元年中，丞相以景帝疾時諸官囚多坐不辜者，而君不任職，免之。
units.en: In the first year of the Jianyuan era, the Chancellor was dismissed on the grounds that during Emperor Jing's illness many imprisoned officials had been wrongly convicted, and he had failed to fulfill his duties.
units.literal: In the middle of the first year of Jianyuan, the Chancellor, because during Emperor Jing's illness various official prisoners many sat not guilty, yet he did not bear his duty, dismissed him.

units.zh: 其後綰卒，子信代。
units.en: Afterward Wan died, and his son Xin succeeded to the title.
units.literal: Afterward Wan died, son Xin succeeded.

units.zh: 坐酎金失侯。
units.en: He was convicted of providing impure ritual gold for the suburban sacrifice and lost his marquisate.
units.literal: He was convicted on account of the tribute gold for the suburban sacrifice and lost his marquisate.

units.zh: 塞侯直不疑者，南陽人也。
units.en: The Marquis of Sai, Zhi Buyi, was a man of Nanyang.
units.literal: The Marquis of Sai Zhi Buyi was a person from Nanyang.

units.zh: 為郎，事文帝。
units.en: He served as a mounted attendant under Emperor Wen.
units.literal: Became mounted attendant, served Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 其同舍有告歸，誤持同舍郎金去，已而金主覺，妄意不疑，不疑謝有之，買金償。
units.en: One of his barracks-mates went home on leave and mistakenly took the gold of another attendant in the same quarters. When the owner discovered the loss, he rashly suspected Buyi. Buyi accepted the blame, purchased gold, and repaid him.
units.literal: His same quarters had someone returning home, mistakenly took the same quarters attendant's gold and left, afterward the gold owner became aware, wildly suspected Buyi, Buyi apologized as having it, bought gold to repay.

units.zh: 而告歸者來而歸金，而前郎亡金者大慚，以此稱為長者。
units.en: Later, the man on leave returned and gave back the gold. The attendant who had lost it was deeply ashamed. For this, Buyi was acclaimed a man of integrity.
units.literal: Then the man on leave returned and gave back the gold, and the attendant who had lost his gold was deeply ashamed; for this Buyi was acclaimed a man of integrity.

units.zh: 文帝稱舉，稍遷至太中大夫。
units.en: Emperor Wen praised and promoted him, and he gradually rose to the rank of Grand Palace Counselor.
units.literal: Emperor Wen praised and promoted, gradually moved to Grand Palace Counselor.

units.zh: 朝廷見，人或毀曰：「不疑狀貌甚美，然獨無柰其善盜嫂何也！」
units.en: At court audiences, some would slander him, saying, "Buyi is very handsome in appearance, yet what can be done about his being adept at stealing his sister-in-law!"
units.literal: At court audiences, some would slander him, saying, "Buyi's appearance is very handsome, yet what can be done about his being adept at stealing his sister-in-law!"

units.zh: 不疑聞，曰：「我乃無兄。」
units.en: When Buyi heard this, he said, "But I have no elder brother."
units.literal: When Buyi heard this, he said, "I have no elder brother at all."

units.zh: 然終不自明也。
units.en: Yet he never once defended himself.
units.literal: Yet ultimately did not explain himself.

units.zh: 吳楚反時，不疑以二千石將兵擊之。
units.en: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Buyi led troops against them in his capacity as a two-thousand-bushel official.
units.literal: When Wu and Chu rebelled, Buyi with two thousand dan led troops to strike them.

units.zh: 景帝後元年，拜為御史大夫。
units.en: In the first year of Emperor Jing's latter reign, he was appointed Imperial Secretary.
units.literal: In the first year of Emperor Jing's reign after Emperor Wen's death, appointed as Imperial Secretary.

units.zh: 天子修吳楚時功，乃封不疑為塞侯。
units.en: The emperor reviewed the merits earned in the Wu-Chu campaign and enfeoffed Buyi as Marquis of Sai.
units.literal: The emperor reviewed the merits from the Wu and Chu campaign and enfeoffed Buyi as Marquis of Sai.

units.zh: 武帝建元年中，與丞相綰俱以過免。
units.en: In the first year of Emperor Wu's Jianyuan era, he was dismissed along with Chancellor Wan on account of their offenses.
units.literal: In the middle of the first year of Emperor Wu's Jianyuan, together with Chancellor Wan both dismissed due to faults.

units.zh: 不疑學老子言。
units.en: Buyi studied the teachings of Laozi.
units.literal: Buyi studied Laozi's teachings.

units.zh: 其所臨，為官如故，唯恐人知其為吏跡也。
units.en: Wherever he was posted, he served in office as before, fearing only that others might discern his traces as an official.
units.literal: Wherever he was assigned, served as official like before, only fearing people know his official traces.

units.zh: 不好立名稱，稱為長者。
units.en: He had no fondness for building a name or reputation, and so was called a man of integrity.
units.literal: Not fond of establishing name and reputation, called a venerable elder.

units.zh: 不疑卒，子相如代。
units.en: When Buyi died, his son Xiangru succeeded to the title.
units.literal: Buyi died, son Xiangru succeeded.

units.zh: 孫望，坐酎金失侯。
units.en: His grandson Wang was convicted of providing impure ritual gold and lost the marquisate.
units.literal: His grandson Wang was convicted on account of the tribute gold for the suburban sacrifice and lost the marquisate.

units.zh: 郎中令周文者，名仁，其先故任城人也。
units.en: The Palace Steward Zhou Wen, whose given name was Ren, had ancestors originally from Rencheng.
units.literal: The Palace Steward Zhou Wen, named Ren, his ancestors were formerly from Rencheng.

units.zh: 以醫見。
units.en: He first came to notice through his skill in medicine.
units.literal: Appeared through medicine.

units.zh: 景帝為太子時，拜為舍人，積功稍遷，孝文帝時至太中大夫。
units.en: When Emperor Jing was still Crown Prince, Ren was appointed as a retainer. Through accumulated merit he was gradually promoted, reaching the rank of Grand Palace Counselor by Emperor Wen's time.
units.literal: When Emperor Jing was crown prince, appointed as retainer, accumulating merit gradually promoted, during Emperor Wen's time reached Grand Palace Counselor.

units.zh: 景帝初即位，拜仁為郎中令。
units.en: When Emperor Jing first ascended the throne, he appointed Ren as Palace Steward.
units.literal: Emperor Jing first ascended, appointed Ren as Palace Steward.

units.zh: 仁為人陰重不泄，常衣敝補衣溺袴，期為不絜清，以是得幸。
units.en: Ren was by nature secretive and discreet, never divulging anything. He habitually wore threadbare patched clothes and soiled trousers, deliberately making himself appear unkempt, and thus won the emperor's favor.
units.literal: Ren as person was deep and heavy not leaking, constantly wore worn patched clothes urine pants, pretended to be not clean and pure, thus obtained favor.

units.zh: 景帝入臥內，於後宮祕戲，仁常在旁。
units.en: When Emperor Jing retired to his private chambers and engaged in secret amusements in the rear palace, Ren was always at his side.
units.literal: Emperor Jing entered sleeping quarters, in the rear palace secret games, Ren constantly at side.

units.zh: 至景帝崩，仁尚為郎中令，終無所言。
units.en: Until Emperor Jing's death, Ren still served as Palace Steward, and to the end he never uttered a word about what he had seen.
units.literal: Until Emperor Jing passed away, Ren still served as Palace Steward, ultimately had nothing to say.

units.zh: 上時問人，仁曰：「上自察之。」
units.en: When the emperor occasionally asked his opinion of people, Ren would say, "Your Majesty should examine them yourself."
units.literal: When the emperor sometimes asked about people, Ren would say, "Your Majesty should examine them yourself."

units.zh: 然亦無所毀。
units.en: Yet neither did he ever slander anyone.
units.literal: Yet also had nothing to slander.

units.zh: 以此景帝再自幸其家。
units.en: For this reason, Emperor Jing twice personally visited his home.
units.literal: With this Emperor Jing twice personally visited his home.

units.zh: 家徙陽陵。
units.en: His family relocated to Yangling.
units.literal: The home moved to Yangling.

units.zh: 上所賜甚多，然常讓，不敢受也。
units.en: The emperor's gifts to him were many, yet he always declined, not daring to accept.
units.literal: What the emperor granted was very many, yet he constantly yielded, not daring to receive.

units.zh: 諸侯群臣賂遺，終無所受。
units.en: Gifts and offerings from feudal lords and ministers he would never accept.
units.literal: Feudal lords and assembled ministers' gifts and remembrances, ultimately received none.

units.zh: 武帝立，以為先帝臣，重之。
units.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he regarded Ren as a minister of the former emperor and treated him with great respect.
units.literal: Emperor Wu ascended, considered him former emperor's minister, honored him.

units.zh: 仁乃病免，以二千石祿歸老，子孫咸至大官矣。
units.en: Ren eventually fell ill and was relieved of his duties, retiring on a salary of two thousand bushels. His sons and grandsons all rose to high office.
units.literal: Ren then fell ill and was dismissed, with two thousand dan salary returned to retire, sons and grandsons all reached high office.

units.zh: 御史大夫張叔者，名歐，安丘侯說之庶子也。
units.en: The Imperial Secretary Zhang Shu, whose given name was Ou, was a concubine's son of the Marquis of Anqiu, Yue.
units.literal: The Imperial Secretary Zhang Shu, named Ou, was the illegitimate son of the Marquis of Anqiu, Yue.

units.zh: 孝文時以治刑名言事太子。
units.en: During Emperor Wen's reign, Ou was known for his command of penal law and legal terminology and reported on affairs to the Crown Prince.
units.literal: During Emperor Wen's reign he was known for expertise in penal law and terminology and presented affairs to the Crown Prince.

units.zh: 然歐雖治刑名家，其人長者。
units.en: Yet although Ou was a practitioner of the Legalist school, he was himself a man of integrity.
units.literal: Yet though Ou governed penal codes school, his person was a venerable elder.

units.zh: 景帝時尊重，常為九卿。
units.en: During Emperor Jing's reign he was respected and honored, regularly serving as one of the Nine Ministers.
units.literal: During Emperor Jing's time respected and honored, constantly became one of the Nine Ministers.

units.zh: 至武帝元朔四年，韓安國免，詔拜歐為御史大夫。
units.en: In the fourth year of Emperor Wu's Yuanshuo era, Han Anguo was dismissed, and an edict was issued appointing Ou as Imperial Secretary.
units.literal: Reached Emperor Wu's the fourth year of Yuanshuo, Han Anguo dismissed, commanded to appoint Ou as Imperial Secretary.

units.zh: 自歐為吏，未嘗言案人，專以誠長者處官。
units.en: From the time Ou first became an official, he never once spoke of prosecuting anyone, devoting himself entirely to administering his office with sincerity and the manner of a man of integrity.
units.literal: Since Ou became official, never once spoke of prosecuting people, specialized in sincerely as venerable elder administering office.

units.zh: 官屬以為長者，亦不敢大欺。
units.en: His subordinates regarded him as a man of integrity and did not dare to deceive him greatly.
units.literal: Subordinates considered him venerable elder, also dared not greatly deceive.

units.zh: 上具獄事，有可卻，卻之；
units.en: When the emperor had prison cases prepared, Ou sent them back whenever they could be returned;
units.literal: When the emperor had prepared prison cases, if they could be sent back, Ou sent them back;

units.zh: 不可者，不得已，為涕泣面對而封之。
units.en: When they could not be sent back, then, having no alternative, he would weep as he faced the prisoner and sealed the verdict.
units.literal: if they could not be sent back, then, having no alternative, he would weep as he faced the prisoner and sealed the verdict.

units.zh: 其愛人如此。
units.en: Such was his compassion for others.
units.literal: His loving people was like this.

units.zh: 老病甐，請免。
units.en: When he grew old and fell ill with dropsy, he requested to be relieved of his duties.
units.literal: Old and ill with dropsy, requested dismissal.

units.zh: 於是天子亦策罷，以上大夫祿歸老于家。
units.en: Thereupon the emperor also issued an edict relieving him of office, and he retired to his home on the salary of a Senior Grand Counselor.
units.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven also issued an edict dismissing him, and he retired home on the salary of a Senior Grand Counselor.

units.zh: 家於陽陵。
units.en: He made his home in Yangling.
units.literal: Made home at Yangling.

units.zh: 子孫咸至大官矣。
units.en: His sons and grandsons all rose to high office.
units.literal: Sons and grandsons all reached high office.

units.zh: 太史公曰：仲尼有言曰「君子欲訥於言而敏於行」，其萬石、建陵、張叔之謂邪？
units.en: The Grand Historian says: Confucius said, "The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech but quick in action." Was this not said of men like the Marquis of Wanshi, Jianling, and Zhang Shu?
units.literal: The Grand Historian says: Confucius had a saying, "The gentleman wishes to be slow of speech but quick in action"—is this not what is meant by the Marquis of Wanshi, Jianling, and Zhang Shu?

units.zh: 是以其教不肅而成，不嚴而治。
units.en: Thus, their instruction achieved its ends without severity, and their governance maintained order without strictness.
units.literal: Therefore, their teaching was not stern yet accomplished, not strict yet governed.

units.zh: 塞侯微巧，而周文處讇君子譏之，為其近於佞也。
units.en: The Marquis of Sai was possessed of subtle skill, while Zhou Wen dwelt in flattery—the gentlemen censured him for bordering on sycophancy.
units.literal: The Marquis of Sai was slightly skillful, yet Zhou Wen resided in flattery—the gentlemen censured him, because he approached sycophancy.

units.zh: 然斯可謂篤行君子矣！
units.en: Yet they may still be called gentlemen of steadfast conduct!
units.literal: Yet these may be called men of steadfast conduct!
